verdict.reason: Rey Cortiço is worth a quick check for after work (16:30 start), but it is not a guaranteed session.  Treat it as a check-first call rather than a sure thing.  Wind is the main thing to watch.  The tide should let the sandbars work without overdoing it.

conversationalSummary.text: TODAY after work (from around 16:30) at Rey Cortiço is the best available bet, but I’m not expecting it to be great given the poor wind angle and weak overall signal. I’d check the Surfline cams and the MEO Beachcam before heading out—if it doesn’t look surprisingly better than what the reports suggest, I’d skip. Low tide is dropping, so it’ll probably come down to how the sandbanks line up rather than raw size. If the cams look decent, then it’s worth a go, otherwise save your energy.

best.explanation: Rey Cortiço looks like a small north coast window for Rare window, Low confidence: 0.3-0.6 m, 28 kJ, 7 s period, lully 1/100, and wind is the main risk.  An open beach break where the sandbanks decide everything; this is best for quiet, punchy peaks when Lagide is too small; 6-9s at low tide can still work on Belgas if the sandbars are lined up, so checking exposed beaches makes sense.  Watch: Surfline consistency is lully; wind angle is poor for this spot.
